subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology — follow-up

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today — good to align on the high-level requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a reproducible benchmark run scheduled: 

Summary of requirements we captured:
- Target latencies: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms for single-turn text-generation at 512 tokens.
- Throughput: sustained 200 reqs/s at concurrency 8 across a single region (us-west).
- Concurrency: expected burst to 32 concurrent requests for 60s during peak syncs; we need to validate graceful degradation.
- Streaming: client requires token-streaming support for partial response display (server-side chunking acceptable).

Benchmark methodology items we discussed (action items in bold):
1) Prompt set: you mentioned ~1.5k prompts covering few-shot summarization, instruction-style completions, and short-chat — please send the canonical set. **(EdgeFin to provide)**
2) Measurement definitions: we will measure p50/p95/p99 response latency from request accepted to first token emitted (for streaming) and to last token emitted (for final latency). Throughput measured as completed responses/sec over a 5 min sustained window. **(Redwood to provide measurement script)**
3) Eval harness: we’ll run a reproducible harness (Docker image + k6 load script) and share the exact commit/seed for RNGs so results are reproducible. **(Redwood will share harness + instructions)**
4) Reproducibility: include hardware profile (GPU type, CPU, networking), model variant (quantization), and batch config in the run artifact.

Attachments: I’ve attached a starting prompt set and our SLO benchmark template. Marcus, Laura — I’ve copied you on infra/benchmark questions below.

Next steps (proposed):
- EdgeFin: upload canonical prompt set and note any streaming-specific prompts by EOD Mon 6/21.
- Redwood: share benchmark harness repo + measurement definitions by Tue 6/22.
- Schedule an initial run week of 6/28 to validate baseline performance.

If that matches your understanding, I’ll create a HubSpot task and share a calendar invite for the week-of run.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0148

Attachments: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl, slo_benchmark_template.xlsx
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>

Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology — follow-up

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Confirming a few clarifications from our side:

1) Prompt set: attaching initial canonical set (edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl). We labeled streaming-sensitive prompts with "stream_hint": true in the metadata. Expect ~1.6k examples after de-dupe.
2) Streaming: our UI expects first token within 150ms for conversational turns where the model generates >64 tokens; otherwise, 250ms is acceptable for short completions. Can Redwood’s measurement scripts capture first-token latency vs. last-token?
3) Model variants: we plan to test two variants — rwd-open-7b (FP16) and rwd-open-7b-q4 (quantized). We will provide model checkpoint refs.

On the run scheduling: week of 6/28 works; can we lock Tuesday 6/29 for the initial baseline? Also need to confirm that Redwood will run both variants back-to-back and share raw latency histograms and per-prompt logs.

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Performance Engineering Lead | EdgeFin
alex.johnson@edgefin.com | +1 206-555-0199

Attachment: edgefin_prompt_set_v1.jsonl
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 00:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology — follow-up

Alex / Marissa —

Appreciate the prompt set. A few technical notes from the runtime side before the run: 

- Measurement definitions: we will capture two distinct timestamps per request: t_request_received, t_first_token_emitted, t_last_token_emitted. From those we compute first-token latency and total-response latency. We will also record service-side queuing time and batch sizes.
- Streaming semantics: Redwood’s streaming SDK flushes token batches at ~16 token granularity by default; we can adjust to smaller granularity (8 tokens) for the streaming-sensitive prompts — this will increase overall token compute by ~3-5% but should help first-token latency. Confirm if EdgeFin prefers smaller flushes for streaming hints.
- Concurrency plan: For the sustained 200 reqs/s target we plan to use 8 server-side worker threads per GPU with a concurrency fanout that maps to the 8 concurrency you requested. For the burst (32) we’ll ensure autoscaler headroom but will also measure tail-latency degradation.

Action items for EdgeFin to confirm:
- Provide the model checkpoint refs you mentioned.
- Confirm whether to prefer smaller streaming flush granularity for streaming_hint prompts.
- If possible, provide a sample of client-side timeout and retry behavior so we mirror realistic client load in the harness.

Marissa — I’ll draft the benchmark harness repo (Dockerfile + k6 script + instrumentation) and push a PR by Monday with the exact commit hash for reproducibility.

Marcus Lin
Principal Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@edgefin.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology — follow-up

Thanks all — quick updates: 

- Model refs: rwd-open-7b@2027-05-10 and rwd-open-7b-q4@2027-05-12 (we'll share S3 paths via a secure transfer).
- Streaming granularity: yes, please test the smaller flush (8 tokens) for prompts with "stream_hint": true — our UX team prefers smoother early partials.
- Client behavior: we use a 5s client timeout with exponential backoff on retry (max 2 retries). We’ll attach a short diagram of retry logic to the Drive folder.

We are happy to lock Tue 6/29 10:00 PT for the baseline run. Alex will share the calendar invite and we’ll check in after the initial run to review histograms and per-prompt failure rates.

Priya
Senior Product Manager | EdgeFin
priya.shah@edgefin.com
